content.title: How long do we keep the raw events?
content.teaser: The models need 90 days. Longer costs storage and means more personal data kept.
content.body:
Raw events are 4.2 million a day. The models and the dashboard only read the last 90 days; everything older lives on in aggregates.

| Keep | Storage | Cost / month |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 days | 38 GB | €1 |
| 90 days | 115 GB | €3 |
| 1 year | 470 GB | €11 |

content.text: Background: on a 13-inch laptop the centered hero shows the headline and the buttons, the shelf only after scrolling.
content.details:
Measured at three window heights:

| Window | Centered: plants visible | Split: app visible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1440 × 900 | half | all of it |
| 1280 × 720 | no | most |
| 390 × 844 | no | after one swipe |

content.text: Does the phone in the split one cost loading time?
No. It is drawn in HTML and CSS, no picture: 6 kB more.
What are the five that are left?
Status page link in the footer, the 404 page, two redirects from the beta domain, and the Safari test. All under an hour except the test.
Neither. Show the app on a phone, with the drawn plants behind it.
Good, that is what people will see first anyway. I am making the new card now.
What??
In short: one colour, two names. The palette says clay, the code says due. Nothing on screen changes; only the variable names in CSS and Swift.
Both pass the test cards (3-D Secure, declined, insufficient funds). Apple Pay shows in both.
And on a small phone? The sheet looks tall.
On a 375-point screen it scrolls by 40 points; the pay button stays pinned at the bottom.
Morning. Plan for the week: pricing on staging, onboarding, then the launch on Monday.

On it. I split it up:

- **landing-page**: the hero and the sections
- **copy**: plan names, buttons, the e-mails
- **onboarding**: sign-up in three steps
- **web-perf** and **e2e-tests** in parallel
- **seo** last

Questions come to your Desk as cards.
Morning reminders at 8:00 are the default now, in the browser’s time zone.
Pricing is on staging with the three plans.
Nice. Where is the checklist?
A page with all 19 items; I tick them off as helpers finish.
Onboarding is on staging: name, first plant, reminder time. 48 seconds on average.
how fast is the landing page on a phone now? and is the plant library in the first load?

content.text:
About **1.4 seconds** on a mid-range phone over 4G.

- first load: 312 kB before, **98 kB** now
- the library: 214 kB, fetched once on the first keystroke, then cached
People keep asking for a summary by mail, by the way.
Then I would send one on Sunday evening. The question is on your Desk.
What blocks Monday?
Only the Safari test, and it is a test problem, not a checkout problem. Monday or Tuesday is on your Desk, with the reasons.

items.text: Working through the last checklist items.

items.title: Run the link checker over staging

content.text: Two heroes are drawn, with the same words. The choice is on your Desk.
Would the split one work on a phone?
Yes: the phone moves under the buttons and the big plant goes. This is the page from top to bottom:
Make the phone a little smaller on laptops.
Done, 10% smaller from 1280 px. Both versions on your Desk again.
Three sets of names for the plans are on your Desk.
Jungle made me smile. Take those.
In: Windowsill, Greenhouse, Jungle. The line under the title is “Start free. Upgrade when the windowsill gets crowded.”
One more: the button on step 1. Both versions are on your Desk, each with its picture.
Step 2 has search and a photo button now. The photo guess is right 4 times out of 5 in our tests.
Keep search first; the camera is slower than typing “fern”.
Search first, the camera as the second button.
When we ask for notifications is the last open point. On your Desk.
Largest paint 1.4 s, first load 98 kB. Info card is on your Desk.
Good enough for Monday.
Then I stop here. Next would be the fonts (42 kB), after the launch.
44 tests: sign-up, first plant, checkout with three test cards, reminders, sharing.

content.text: 41 of 44 green; the Safari checkout test fails 2 of 12 runs, always on the iframe. Question on your Desk.
Titles, descriptions and the sitemap are in. 31 pages.
The social card is on your Desk: photo or illustration.
Reworking it as you said: the app on a phone, drawn plants behind.
Goal for 1.2: widgets, dark mode, sharing. In review by Friday.
Helpers: **widgets**, **push-reminders**, **app-store**, and **crash-triage** once TestFlight runs.
Sharing is in, invite by link or QR code.
Build 418 is on TestFlight, 1,240 testers.
what is the widget crash, and do we have to wait for it?

items.text: It crashes when the time zone changes while the timeline reloads: the date math runs on a stale calendar.

content.text: The crash is in the widget timeline on a time-zone change; **419 fixes it** and is on TestFlight since noon. Holding 1.2 for it costs one day of review. Card on your Desk.
App Store text is ready; the release notes are a page in Artifacts.
Timeline refresh every 30 minutes, inside the iOS budget.
Both sizes designed. Which first is on your Desk.
Can the medium one tick off a plant without opening the app?
Yes, with an App Intent on iOS 17 and later. 96% of the testers are on 17+.
Due plants now come in one notification: “Water the fern and the pilea”.
Testing time-zone changes for the daily time.
Four screenshots for the 6.9-inch size; the others are scaled.
Which go first is on your Desk.
Three crash groups in build 418. The widget one is the only frequent one.
419 has the widget fix. PlantPhotoCache is next; it needs a device with little storage to reproduce.
I want one source for colours and type, for the web and for iOS.
Tokens in one JSON file, built into CSS variables and a Swift file. **tokens**, **icons** and **dark-mode** work on it.
Tokens v0.9 are in both apps.
The tab bar icons in three styles are on your Desk; the whole set follows the pick.
tokens.json builds into tokens.css and Tokens.swift; CI fails when they drift.
Proposal: name colours by their job in code. First one on your Desk.
Explained on the card.
All 48 icons drawn in outline on a 24 grid, 2 px stroke.
Tab bar in three styles on your Desk.
Every screen has a dark version; the plant colours stay.
Only the photos are open: on your Desk.
Renewals are failing? I got an e-mail from Stripe.
Yes: since the 14:02 deploy every webhook gets a 400. Stripe retries, nothing is lost yet. Rollback question on your Desk, critical.
Rolled back. 212 events replayed, every renewal reconciled. The report:
Smart retries for two weeks now: failed renewals 4.1% → 1.3%.
Checkout must be ready for the web launch on Monday.
It is built twice, as a sheet and as a page; **checkout** put both on your Desk. **load-test** runs k6 against staging once you allow it.

content.text: Retries: day 1, day 3, day 7. On your Desk.
The webhook route keeps the raw body now, tested through the real middleware.
Sheet and page both done, test cards pass.
Which one do you prefer?
The sheet: people come from the plant list and go back to it.
Invoices are PDFs with a number per country series.
What people may change themselves is on your Desk.
VAT rates for all 27 EU countries come from Stripe Tax now.
One question left: VAT included everywhere?
400 rps with p95 176 ms. Info card on your Desk.

I want a retention dashboard: do people keep watering after week one?
Pipeline: apps → collector → dbt models → dashboard, hourly.
Dashboard is live, refreshed hourly.
why is the cdc-sync 40 minutes behind?

items.text: The backfill for the dashboard wrote a lot of WAL; Debezium reads it all.

content.text: The backfill wrote **140 GB of WAL** today and the sync reads all of it. It catches up by tonight; the backfill is done. It also fills the primary disk: **infra** has a card about that.
How long to keep raw events is on your Desk; I merged the CDC schedule question into it.
The collector validates every event against the schema; bad ones go to a dead-letter bucket.
IP and e-mail are dropped; country is kept.
Renamed to fct_sessions.
57 tests, all green.
Dashboard is up.
Why is the active count higher than I thought?
Because opening the app counts. With “watered a plant” it is 14,960. Which one is on your Desk.
Two things: a second region for the Americas, and a smaller bill.

Plan: us-east with a read replica, Kubernetes 1.33 first, then the bill. Eight helpers: **terraform**, **k8s-upgrade**, **postgres-replica**, **cdn**, **backups**, **observability**, **cost**, **secrets**.
The bill comes down by €2,380 a month from December.
